assumptions.statement: Labor available for water recovery must be checked against baseline available_commons_hours and hours_per_resident from simulation data to prevent hidden burden.
Release authority modeling must not assume explicit legal authority exists; dependencies must be declared pending validation.

expected_effects.rationale: Explicit modeling of authority and isolation unblocks recovery review.
Modeling authority testing requires explicit labor allocation rather than shifting to resident burden.
Does not assume emergency power sunset is defined; leaves governance warnings explicit.

hypothesis: Water recovery can move from blocked to testable if source isolation, alternate supply, lab testing, and release authority are modeled explicitly against baseline labor availability and governance warnings.

queries: CIaC water public health warning interventions expected effects labor energy privacy public health governance accessibility scenario resilience

risk_tradeoffs.mitigation: Model delivered water fallback and conservative no-release default.
risk_tradeoffs.risk: Testing authority may be unavailable during disruption

risk_tradeoffs.mitigation: Enforce labor rotation and cross-training from baseline_90d_simulation.json maintenance_hours.
risk_tradeoffs.risk: Labor allocation for water safety may exceed available_commons_hours

acceptance_tests: No new survival-critical unmet demand is introduced.
No labor is shifted into untracked resident burden.
Privacy, consent, public-health, accessibility, and governance assumptions remain explicit.

title: Water recovery test-and-release playbook with labor governance
